correctness.rationale: All split graphs on zero through seven vertices are covered by looping over each clique size and every binary cross-incidence mask. Joint n-round refinement and exhaustive adjacency-preserving bijection tests found 1,1,2,4,9,21,56,164 equivalence groups and zero collisions; positive-order numbers independently agree with Royle (2000), Table 1. The eight-vertex pair has equal equitable quotients (clique size four, independent size four; quotient neighbor counts (3,2) and (2,0)) but nonisomorphic independent-neighborhood multisets (all distinct versus duplicated pairs). Adding t universal vertices preserves splitness, connectedness, logical indistinguishability and nonisomorphism for every t>=0. Source code rerun from the actual package path with terminal PASS. The infinite statement does not rest on finite experiments.

value.rationale: First class-relative failure order for C2 is a natural exact invariant of a standard hereditary graph class; minimality is established exhaustively, not guessed from one example. The explicit eight-vertex incidence-cycle obstruction and a connected witness for every n>=8 show a sharp and persistent limitation of colour refinement in a class used for structured graph isomorphism testing. Royle's enumerative counts provide independent validation and the result offers a precise benchmark for stronger logical/algorithmic methods, not an arbitrary slice of a parameter.
